idiom_name: first-class function passed to or stored by the context (object map for named strategies)
implementation_notes: Functions are first-class values in JavaScript, so the strategy interface collapses into a function and the context simply holds or receives it: processPayment(strategy, amount) or an object property set from outside. Array.prototype.sort taking a compare function is the pattern in the language itself, and the idiomatic registry form is a plain object mapping names to functions ({ 'credit-card': payWithCreditCard, ... }) which replaces the if/else chain with one lookup - keep the lookup table and the selection in one place, not scattered across call sites. The class-per-strategy form is only worth its ceremony when the strategy carries configuration or exposes several operations; even then a factory function returning a closure (partial application) is usually enough.
pitfalls: A plain object lookup returns undefined for an unknown key: strategies['BigBulk'] is not a function and fails later at the call site, so validate the lookup (or use a Map plus an explicit error) at the boundary.
Passing a method as a strategy loses its receiver (arr.map(obj.method) throws on this); bind it (obj.method.bind(obj)) or use an arrow-function property.

Closures keep their captured environment alive: a strategy closing over a large object or a DOM node pins it for as long as the context holds the function, which turns a small leak into a long-lived one.
